item.text: {"reviews":[{"benchmark":"arc","instrument_review":"ARC-AGI-2 is reviewed using the supplied EFPA Test Review Model 2025, version 5.0, attributed to EFPA, https://www.efpa.eu/, CC BY-SA 4.0. Only the supplied benchmark passages and model extraction were used; the authoritative PDF was not inspected. Ratings retain EFPA meanings: n/a = inapplicable; 0 = insufficient evidence; 1 = inadequate; 2 = adequate; 3 = good; 4 = excellent. Section judgments are qualitative, not averaged; no aggregate quality score is calculated. Final evaluation: public grid tasks and specified scoring support examination of performance under recorded conditions. Development procedures and scoring examples are strengths; public exposure, material corrections and unresolved AI score precision limit interpretation. Reliability and validity are critical attributes rated 0, so EFPA guidance restricts use to research or exceptional circumstances involving highly skilled experts; this is an evidence limitation, not demonstrated poor performance. Conclusions: use for research comparisons of grid-task performance, with expertise in evaluation conditions, scoring and exposure risks. Broad intelligence claims and small differences between systems remain unsupported by this packet; supplier qualification requirements and future research plans are not supplied.","supported_claims":["1: Name and short name: ARC-AGI-2. Developers: ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners; individual authors, adaptation authors, local distributor, original publisher and publication dates are not fully identified. ARC Prize runs or verifies the evaluations described. Current and previous review dates are unspecified; source inspection was 7 October 2026.","2.1: Other—rule induction, grid problem solving, abstract reasoning. These describe the stated targets, not established latent traits.","2.2: Other—AI research and system comparison. No human clinical, educational or occupational assessment use is stated.","2.3: Intended assessed population: AI systems solving unfamiliar grid problems. Human participants supplied development evidence, not the target AI reference population.","2.4: Main intended users: researchers comparing AI systems, inferred from the stated use; no formal user classification is supplied.","2.5: One overall problem-averaged score is described; no separate scores are established as distinct skills.","2.6: Other—AI-generated output grids submitted to software. Costs and times are described as released outputs, not demonstrated score components.","2.10: Coloured two-dimensional grids with worked input-output examples. The packet does not establish whether every AI receives images, serialized text or another encoding.","2.11: 1,000 development problems and three evaluation sets of 120 problems each. Problems can contain multiple new inputs; minimum, maximum and typical input counts are unspecified.","2.12.1: Individual AI-system administration is the closest interpretation; group administration is not described.","2.12.2: Public problems are openly accessible; ARC Prize verified testing controls settings and budgets. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions; AI equivalence is not demonstrated.","2.16: Static problem sets are described. Adaptive generation, adaptive selection and randomized forms are not established.","2.17: Other—the assessed AI produces responses; human solvers informed development. This is performance testing, not human self-report.","3.1: Digital scoring of submitted AI responses.","3.2: Each new input earns 1 if either permitted attempt exactly matches answer dimensions and colours, otherwise 0. It offers development problems and three evaluation sets with differing access. Its stated purpose is comparison of unfamiliar grid problem solving, with broader reasoning aspirations. Scoring permits two attempts per input and averages exact-match credits within and across problems. No human or AI normative score tables are supplied.","6.1.1 = 2; 6.2.1 = 3: The target of inferring new rules from examples and the reasons for compositional, low-specialist-knowledge puzzles are explained.
